FT: 🇲🇽 Mexico 2-0 South Africa 🇿🇦 #WorldCup2026 is officially open. And it did NOT disappoint.
Let's be honest — nobody expected THAT second half.
What happened:
Mexico controlled this from minute one. Quiñones capitalised on a howler from Sithole in the 9th minute and El Tri never looked back. Dominant possession, chance after chance — keeper Ronwen Williams was South Africa's best player by a mile. WikipediaESPN
Then the second half turned into an absolute circus. Sithole — the same man who gifted Mexico the first goal — got himself sent off for a reckless foul on Gutiérrez, leaving South Africa with 10 men. Then Zwane got a second red for South Africa in the 84th minute. Mexico's Cesar Montes also walked — making it 9 vs 10 at one point. Pure madness at the Azteca. 
The numbers told the story early:Mexico 57% possession. xG: Mexico 0.66 — South Africa 0.06. Shots on goal 2-1. Duels won 25-12. South Africa were never really in this game. ESPN
The bigger picture:
Sithole could end up playing just 50 minutes of the entire tournament — scored an own goal AND got himself suspended. One of the worst individual World Cup debuts in recent memory. Yahoo Sports
For Mexico though — job done. Home crowd delivered. The Azteca remains unbeaten in World Cup football — 7 games, 0 losses. That ground is genuinely haunted in the best possible way. Fox News
What this means going forward:
Mexico top of Group A. South Africa in crisis — still looking for their first ever knockout round appearance and now depleted for their next game. Yahoo Sports
16 years ago same fixture, same stadium, same manager — ended 1-1. Tonight Mexico made sure history didn't repeat.
The World Cup is HERE and it's already delivering chaos, red cards, and history.
What a night. ⚽🌍🔥

Chances of winning:

They were 15-25 when they saw him cry in the 2016 Copa America final after coming short again in their 3rd consecutive international final.
They saw his own people burning his jerseys and cuss him for not being able to end their trophy drought.
They saw the country’s footballing idol tell the team to not come back to Argentina if they failed to lose that final.
They watched their idol carry the blame for every defeat and never complain about it.
They saw him fall, get back up, and try again.
Over. And. Over.

FOUR consecutive international titles isn’t by coincidence.
Messi inspired an entire generation of footballers that are willing to go to war for him in every match.
Simply because they don’t want to see their idol fall again.

Yesterday, Curacao secured a battling draw against Ecuador. 

The team on the pitch. The fans in the stands. And the people back home, all celebrated like they had won the World Cup. 

Which in many ways they had. 

Because, as always, context is everything. 

Curacao is the smallest nation ever to participate in the World Cup. With a head count just over 1, 50, 000 people; it hosts fewer people than those usually stuck at the Andheri Saki Naka traffic jam. 

That draw, also made them the smallest nation ever to win a point at the World Cup. Remarkable on all counts. Even more special, considering they had been beaten 1-7 by Germany in their first game. 

Perhaps this also goes to show beyond the pitch, how we are all on different life journeys. 

A draw for one person might be nothing short of an epic win for someone else. This is not just about football. 

Our milestones are different. Our constraints do not match. Our dreams are wonderfully diverse. 

To use the relevant pun: We all chase different goals. 

And yet, we are united in the sense of unabashed joy we feel in scoring them.
